subject: how to tell scantwo which scanone to use for

messages.author: 327a8e5641d73ebe
messages.subject: how to tell scantwo which scanone to use for
parts:
Hi,
 
The help file (new summary scantwo Oct 2006) says that scantwo uses the output of the single qtl model from scanone.  I have run multiple scantwo and scanone analyses using Haley-Knott regression, EM, and multiple imputation.  How do I know if my scantwo output (say from multiple imputations) is using the correct scanone output (also from multiple imputations)?  Do I need to use particular filenames or run these analyses back to back?
 
thanks
 
Tarek
 
***************************************

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: how to tell scantwo which scanone to use for
parts:
Scantwo also performs the relevant single-dimensional scan with
scanone, so the results contain the relevant scanone results. There
are no worries about object or file names or such.

karl

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Re: how to tell scantwo which scanone to use for
parts:
R/qtl (available at http://www.rqtl.org) uses classical methods.
For Bayesian multiple QTL mapping, consider the R/qtlbim package
(available at http://www.qtlbim.org).

The R/qtlbim package is distinct from R/qtl, but some of the same data
formats, and relies on R/qtl for some things (such as data import).

regards,
karl
